description: Adds annotations (arrows, boxes, text, blur, steps, spotlight, magnifier, pen, highlight) to a screenshot or a recording. Non-destructive: the original is kept and the user can open the editor or clip window and keep editing or undo. Coordinates are original pixels (a recording's source pixels) with a top-left origin; geometry is clamped to the frame. At most 200 annotations per call. Screenshots: if the capture is open in the editor the call is refused: ask the user to close that window. Recordings: each item may also have start and end seconds (shown from start up to, not including, end; default the whole clip; end is clamped to the duration and must be greater than start); the clip window updates live and its Undo removes the annotation. Blur and redact cover their area on every frame they show, and cover it completely if they can't be drawn. Returns the updated preview (for a recording, a frame with the annotations drawn) and the stored annotations with their ids.

description: Schedules a draft (with an image) to post to X at a time, ISO 8601 like 2026-12-01T09:30:00Z. At least 5 minutes ahead (earlier times are moved to 5 minutes from now). Needs the user's own X app connected, and X bills them directly when it runs. Public, so it asks the user first (status "awaiting_approval", then get_request_status). Uses ScreenPost's scheduler and its crash-safe submission rules.

description: Makes a connected X account the default: the one posts use when no account is given. account is its handle (with or without @) or user ID; an unknown account is an error (see get_status for the connected handles). It changes where later posts go, so it never runs on the agent's say-so: it returns status "awaiting_approval" and a requestId, ScreenPost asks the user (even with "Allow without asking"; policy "Never" denies it), and get_request_status reports the outcome. description: Starts recording the screen to the library (an MP4). Non-interactive by default: mode "full" records a display (displayId, default the one under the pointer), "window" needs windowId, "area" needs rect in points from the display's top-left; with interactive: true ScreenPost shows its own selector for the user. Optional audio {system, mic}, showFrame (outline the recorded area while recording; default the user's setting; the outline is never in the video) and maxSeconds (10 to 1200; default 120). It is never silent: a notice appears and the menu-bar icon shows "agent". If the user turned on "Ask before agents take screenshots" it asks first, and recording with the microphone ALWAYS asks (status "awaiting_approval", then get_request_status). Returns a recordingId; stop it with stop_recording. Only one recording at a time. Needs Screen Recording permission.

description: Steps back through the edits made by agent tools on this capture (default 1 step, up to the 30 most recent). Refuses if the capture was edited in the editor since, so the user's work isn't discarded. Refused if the editor has the capture open. For a recording it steps back the clip's own edit history, the same one the clip window's Undo uses (trim, Beautify, annotations, including edits the user made there): that history is kept while ScreenPost runs and is gone after a relaunch (the edits stay). Steps an agent made are undone at once; a step the user made in the clip window returns status "awaiting_approval" and the user is asked first, with the step named. redo brings a step back.

description: Sends a capture (image, video or GIF) from the user's Mac to an https URL with PUT or POST, streaming the file: for presigned upload URLs such as Timetopost's prepare_media_upload. It leaves the Mac, so it asks the user, and the sheet shows the destination host. Only https URLs on public hostnames are accepted (no IP addresses, localhost, private ranges or other ports), and redirects to a different host are never followed. The raw file bytes are sent (not base64), and ScreenPost adds no credentials or cookies of its own: a presigned URL needs none. Optional headers (for example x-amz-*) are sent as given and never logged. Returns {status, bytes, contentType}; a non-2xx status is a failure (a 403 usually means the presigned link expired: request a new one and retry).

clientRequestId.description: Optional idempotency key. Retrying with the same value returns the first result instead of repeating the action.

contentType.description: Content-Type to send, for example image/png, image/gif or video/mp4 (default: the file's own type). Must match the type the presigned URL was prepared for.
